title: `:help` in a sandbox's Neovim fails with an error because the vimdoc parser never loads
foundBy: session agent, while checking SBX-108's trimmed parser list in the shipped image
details:
Running `:help` in a sandbox's Neovim prints `E5113: … Parser could not be created for buffer 2 and language "vimdoc"`. A buffer whose filetype is `query` fails the same way. Neovim's own ftplugins for both start treesitter without a guard.

Neovim bundles the vimdoc, vim, query, lua, c and markdown parsers in /usr/local/lib/nvim/parser. At startup lazy.nvim resets the runtimepath and leaves that directory out, so none of the bundled parsers are found. Under `nvim --clean` the same parsers load. The config installs its own lua, c and markdown parsers through nvim-treesitter, which is why only vimdoc and query show the error.

Reproduce in ghcr.io/codesweep-ai/sandbox:v0.0.0-20260929195333-38b6867ec3dd with `HOME=/sandbox/home nvim --headless +help +qa!`.

A fix puts /usr/local/lib/nvim back on the runtimepath through lazy.nvim's `performance.rtp.paths`, or installs vimdoc and query alongside the other parsers. The first also lets SBX-108's list drop its own lua parser.
